t: Sum of Values at Indices With K Set Bits
o: Sum nums[i] over indices whose binary representation has exactly k ones. With indices < 1000 (≤ 10 bits), computing popcount per index via bit tricks or bin(i).count('1') is trivial. Example 1: indices 1 (001), 2 (010), 4 (100) have one set bit → 10+1+2 = 13. Example 2: only index 3 (11) has two set bits → 1.
k: Popcount via Brian Kernighan loop or builtin; indices fit in 10 bits.

a.i: Iterate indices, compute the number of set bits, accumulate matching elements.
s: For each i, compute pc = popcount(i).
If pc == k, add nums[i] to the answer.
a.t: O(n log n)-ish — popcount is O(bits) per index, effectively O(n)

a.i: Same logic without builtins: repeatedly strip the lowest set bit (Brian Kernighan) to count bits — portable across languages lacking popcount intrinsics.
s: For each index, count bits by x &= x−1 until zero.
a.t: O(n · bits) — bit loop per index

w: Trivial; edge cases include k = 0 (only index 0 qualifies) and k larger than any index's bit count (answer 0). Follow-up: sum over a range of indices with popcount ≡ k mod m, solvable with digit DP.
